state: Finite slices of i32-coordinate points under ordinary allocation-success Rust execution.
cost: O(n log n) comparisons, O(n) stack work and auxiliary memory; unmeasured wall-clock cost.
forward: Sort and deduplicate points, construct lower/upper strict-left-turn chains, concatenate without repeated endpoints. Return canonical extreme vertices counterclockwise.
inverse: behavior_complement: Exclude absent-source vertices, nonminimal first point, repeats, clockwise/non-strict polygon turns, or input strictly right of an edge. For a segment exclude off-line points or points beyond endpoints. Empty output requires empty input.

reverse_reconstruction: For canonical strict convex polygon H, compatible inputs are finite sequences containing every H vertex, with remaining points inside/on H, arbitrary order/multiplicity. Segment output admits points on its closed segment containing both ends. Singleton admits nonempty repetitions; empty admits only empty. Length and interior data are not recoverable.
metamorphic_relation: Permutation or duplication preserves output since sorted distinct support is unchanged.

metamorphic_relation: Positive uniform integer scaling k and translation t, with all images in i32, maps H to kH+t and preserves its canonical start. Reflection requires reversing orientation and recanonicalization.
fixed_point: H(H(P))=H(P); its extreme vertices have identical convex support, and collinear interior points cannot return.

support_relation: For every integer direction d, max dot(d,P)=max dot(d,H(P)) on nonempty input. Strict turns, source membership, supporting edges and minimal start certify polygons; degenerates require separate conditions.

state_invariant: Each processed sorted prefix has a lower-boundary stack with strict positive consecutive turns. Each point is pushed once and popped at most once per chain. Reversal builds the upper boundary; dropping terminal endpoints prevents repeated joins.

range_bound: Each coordinate difference magnitude <=2^32-1; product <=(2^32-1)^2; cross magnitude <=2(2^32-1)^2<2^65. Widening before subtraction gives exact i128 predicates. Allocation failure is not a Result.
checks: Debug/release twice; strict Clippy; compiled mutant; source-bound syntax twice.
limitations: Finite observations are not universal verification; allocator exhaustion untested; syntax projection lacks semantic type resolution and macro expansion. Exact implementation has no approximate execution profile.
